title: On-call playbook: rotations, handoffs, runbooks, and simulation scenarios
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference’s operational practices for on-call rotations, shift handoffs, severity-based runbooks, postmortem structure, game-day exercises, and customer-facing status updates. It is intended for SREs, platform engineers, and on-call product owners.

Table of contents:
1) Purpose and scope
2) Incident lifecycle and responsibilities
3) Severity definitions and SLO triggers
4) Runbooks (severity-based) - quick reference table + detailed steps
5) On-call rotations, handoffs, and escalation etiquette
6) Postmortem template and timelines
7) Game-day scenarios and grading rubric
8) Status page and customer comms templates
9) Appendix: links, commands, and ownership

1) Purpose and scope
- Purpose: Provide a single source of truth for responding to production incidents that affect availability, latency, or correctness of Redwood’s inference services.
- Scope: Applies to hosted API, Dedicated, and Private control-plane components (services listed in section 8). Excludes non-prod CI jobs unless they directly impact customer-facing traffic.
- Audience: On-call SREs, service owners, platform engineers, incident commanders, and support escalation engineers.

2) Incident lifecycle and responsibilities
High-level phases (ordered):
1. Detection & Triage: Alert arrives in PagerDuty -> primary on-call acknowledges within SLA (see section 3).
2. Mobilize: Determine scope, severity, and initial mitigations; declare Incident in Incident Command if Severity P1/P0.
3. Stabilize: Execute runbook steps to reduce customer impact (fallbacks, scaling, model switch).
4. Communicate: Update internal channels and status page.
5. Recover: Restore normal operations and validate with metrics.
6. Review: Postmortem and follow-up action items assigned.

Key roles and responsibilities:
- Primary on-call (SRE): Initial acknowledgement, triage, and first mitigation.
- Secondary/Support: Deeper debugging, failover, data access.
- Incident Commander (IC): Coordinate cross-team actions for high-severity incidents, own communication cadence.
- Service Owner: Approves rollbacks, model/policy changes, and post-incident fixes.
- Communications Owner (Customer Success or IC): Publishes official customer-facing messages on the status page.

3) Severity definitions and SLO triggers
- P0 / Sev 0 (Critical): System-wide outage affecting >50% of customers or API error-rate > 10% for 10+ minutes. Action: declare Incident Command in 10 minutes, page leadership.
- P1 / Sev 1 (High): Significant degradation (e.g., 20-50% customers impacted, latency SLO violations for a key route). Action: page primary and secondary, aim to mitigate within 30 minutes.
- P2 / Sev 2 (Medium): Single-region or single-service degradation, partial feature loss. Action: page primary only, escalate if >2 hours unresolved.
- P3 / Sev 3 (Low): Minor issues, non-customer-facing alerts, or cosmetic. Action: create ticket and handle in normal backlog.

Example SLOs (service-level):
- inference-api (text-generation): Availability 99.9% monthly; latency p95 < 350ms for seq_len<=512.
- embeddings-service: Availability 99.8% monthly; tail latency p99 < 700ms.
- health-checks: Probe up >= 99.95%.

Error budget thresholds that trigger action:
- If monthly error budget used > 25% and trending up -> SRE-led investigation.
- If > 50% consumed -> immediate executive notification and priority remediation.

4) Runbooks (severity-based)
Quick reference table:
| Runbook ID | Symptom(s) | Primary responder | Escalation | Immediate target | Location |
| OR-101 | inference-api 5xx spike | oncall-primary-api | secondary-sre / model-team | reduce 5xx to baseline in 30m | /runbooks/OR-101 |
| OR-102 | latency p95 > 500ms | oncall-primary-api | infra-scheduler | restore p95 < 400ms in 45m | /runbooks/OR-102 |
| OR-201 | KV cache cold-start | oncall-cache | runtime-team | restore hit-rate > 80% | /runbooks/OR-201 |
| OR-301 | autoscaler thrash | oncall-platform | infra-ops | stabilize autoscaler, stop flapping | /runbooks/OR-301 |

Detailed runbook example (OR-101: inference-api 5xx spike):
- Invocation criteria: sudden jump in 5xx across multiple routes or Datadog alert "inference-api.5xx.rate" > 0.10 for 5 minutes.
- Initial steps (first 10 minutes):
  1) Acknowledge the PagerDuty alert.
  2) Check Datadog dashboard: https://datadog.internal/redwood/inference-api (look at 1m/5m windows).
  3) Run quick health checks: curl -sS -D - https://inference-api.prod.redwood.com/health | head -n 20
  4) Check recent deploys: gitops commit /deployments/inference-api; run `kubectl rollout status deployment/inference-api -n prod`
  5) If errors correlate to a deploy within the last 15m, consider rollback: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/inference-api -n prod --to-revision=<previous>` (get approval from service-owner if rollback affects client contracts).
- Mitigation steps (10-45 minutes):
  - Route traffic to warm model variant (route policy: inference-api -> model: gpt-j-6b-quantized-warm) by updating routing override in control plane: `redwoodctl route update --service inference-api --variant gpt-j-6b-quantized-warm`
  - Increase replica count for short window: `kubectl scale deployment/inference-api --replicas=12 -n prod` (observe autoscaler interactions).
  - If 5xx comes from backend (kv-cache or storage): open connection diagnostics: `ss -tuna | grep inference-api` and check Redis metrics.
- Validation (after mitigation):
  - Ensure 5xx rate drops below baseline and p95 latency meets SLO for 10 consecutive minutes.
  - Announce status in #ops-oncall and update Incident doc.
- Post-incident actions:
  - Create ticket in JIRA (INC-<number>) with root cause hypothesis and follow-ups assigned to Service Owner.
  - Mark for postmortem if P1/P0.

Runbook notes and safe defaults:
- If unsure, fall back to conservative traffic routing (route to smaller model or reduce max_tokens).
- Avoid rolling restarts of multiple services at once; coordinate with IC.

5) On-call rotations, handoffs, and escalation etiquette
Rotation model:
- Primary rotation cadence: 7-day primary shifts (Mon 08:00 -> Mon 08:00 local).
- Secondary rotation cadence: weekly, aligned with primary.
- Coverage model: primary + secondary + follow-the-sun on-call for APAC (regional escalation list).
- Paging policy: page primary on P1/P0 and secondary on P1 if primary is unavailable for >5 minutes.

On-call responsibilities checklist (start of shift):
- Confirm PagerDuty is active and contact methods are correct.
- Read the recent incident log (sheet link) for ongoing issues.
- Verify personal access: kubectl, redwoodctl, Datadog.
- Check scheduled maintenance windows and tickets that may cause noise.

Handoff checklist (end-of-shift):
1) Summary of incidents handled during shift (INC numbers + short summaries).
2) Ongoing mitigations and next steps (links to runbook or task list).
3) Any pager backlog or noisy alerts and adjusted thresholds.
4) Confirm on-call rotation change in PagerDuty and post a short note in #ops-oncall: "handoff: primary -> <name> (UTC tz)".

Escalation etiquette:
- Use Slack channels by priority: #ops-oncall (realtime debugging), #incident-command (IC coordination), #customer-notifications (publish drafts).
- Keep messages concise and include severity, impact, hypothesis, and next action.
- Avoid public blame; focus on facts and remediation.

6) Postmortem template and timelines
When to run a postmortem:
- Required for all P0/P1 incidents and optional for P2 where substantial customer impact occurred.
Postmortem timeline:
- Draft within 48 hours of incident resolution.
- Triage review within 5 business days.
- Final published postmortem with action owner assignments within 10 business days.

Postmortem structure (required sections):
- Title: short, factual (e.g., "P1: inference-api 5xx regression after model rollout - 2026-01-22").
- Incident summary: time window, affected services, customer impact, severity.
- Timeline: minute-level events from detection to resolution.
- Root cause analysis: technical cause, contributing factors (human/process/tools).
- Mitigation: what was done to restore.
- Corrective actions (ACOs): owner, due date, verification plan.
- Lessons learned: changes to runbooks, monitoring, or release processes.
- Metrics and attachments: dashboards, logs, pagedecisions, links.

Example corrective action item format:
- ACO-123: Add a redundant health-check on inference-router to detect slow-start conditions. Owner: @Diego Alvarez. Due: 2026-03-01. Verification: bench tests, run in canary for 2 weeks.

7) Game-day scenarios and grading rubric
Purpose: Validate culture, runbooks, and tooling without customer impact. Run quarterly (minimum) with cross-team participation.
Typical game-day scenarios (each ~2 hours):
- Scenario A: Model variant rollout causing increased 5xxs (objectives: identify rollback procedure, validate routing overrides).
- Scenario B: KV cache cold-start after cluster reboot (objectives: restore hit rate, validate cache warming strategy).
- Scenario C: Autoscaler misconfiguration causes oscillation under load (objectives: stabilize scaling policy, tune HPA).
- Scenario D: Private deployment control plane network partition with one customer (objectives: validate fallback to local model serving and customer communication).

Grading rubric (pass/fail metrics):
- Time-to-detect < 10 minutes (detection play).
- Time-to-mitigate partial impact < 30 minutes for P1-like scenario.
- Communication cadence: first internal update within 15 minutes; public/update on status page within 30 minutes.
- After-action: post-game report with 3 ACOs and at least one automation improvement.

Game-day logistics and roles:
- Organizer: SRE lead schedules scenario, provides verifier.
- Participants: primary/secondary on-call, service owners, customer success, platform.
- IC for scenario: assigned at start, acts as conductor.

8) Status page and customer communication templates
Status page ownership: Customer Success + Incident Commander. Use Status.io (internal namespace).
Publication cadence for P1/P0:
- Initial: within 30 minutes with impact scope and mitigation work in progress.
- Follow-up: every 60 minutes or on material changes.
- Resolved: within 60 minutes of mitigation completion with resolution and next steps.

Templates (copy/paste and edit):
- Initial (short):
  Title: "Investigating: Intermittent 5xx errors for inference API"
  Body: "We are currently investigating increased 5xx errors affecting text-generation API requests. Some customers may see failures or degraded performance. Our on-call team has been mobilized and we are working on mitigations. We will provide an update within 30 minutes. Affected service: inference-api. Impact: failed requests and increased latency for some customers."

- Follow-up (technical update):
  Title: "Update: ongoing investigation into inference API 5xx"
  Body: "We have identified that the issue correlates with a recent model rollout to variant gpt-j-6b-quantized. We have temporarily routed traffic to a previous stable variant and are monitoring. Error rates have decreased from ~12% -> ~3% over the last 10m. Next update in 30-60 minutes."

- Resolved (final):
  Title: "Resolved: inference API 5xx spike"
  Body: "The incident impacting inference API has been resolved. Root cause: model rollout that caused memory pressure on some nodes; mitigation included reverting the rollout and increasing replica memory limits for the model pool. No customer data was exposed. Postmortem will be published when complete. If you continue to see errors, please contact support@redwood.com."

Internal incident doc template (short):
- Incident ID: INC-
- Severity: 
- IC: 
- Timeline (UTC): detection, mitigation, recovery
- Actions taken: list with timestamps and links to commands/rollbacks
- Next steps / ACOs: list with owners and dates

9) Appendix: links, commands, and ownership
Service owners and contacts (primary):
- inference-api: @Marco Chen (service-owner-inference)
- embeddings-service: @Evelyn Roberts
- kv-cache (redis-cluster): @Diego Alvarez
- autoscaler/hpa: @Priya Nambiar

Useful links and internal tools:
- Datadog inference dashboards: https://datadog.internal/redwood/inference-api
- PagerDuty rotation and escalation: https://pagerduty.internal/redwood/oncall
- Incident tracker (JIRA filter): https://jira.internal/redwood/issues/?filter=incident
- Runbooks folder: https://confluence.internal/redwood/runbooks/oncall
- Status page editor: https://status.internal.redwood/overview

Helpful commands:
- `kubectl get pods -n prod -l service=inference-api -o wide`
- `redwoodctl route list --service inference-api`
- `redwoodctl logs --service inference-api --since 15m | grep ERROR`
- `redis-cli -h redis-prod-01 info memory`

Document maintenance and review cadence:
- Owner (Engineering): oncall-sre-team.
- Review cadence: annually or after any P0/P1 postmortem.
- Game-days: quarterly; one must include a Private deployment scenario each year.

If you need help: ping @oncall-sre or open a ticket in #ops-oncall and the on-call lead will triage.

-- End of playbook --
